question_text:
The coercivity $\left(H_{\mathrm{C}}\right)$ of a sample of a material known as grain-oriented steel is $300 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{m}$. The saturation magnetization ( $\mu_0 M_{\mathrm{S}}$ ) of this material is 2.1 T . A hysteresis loop for this material was measured to determine the properties.

1. If the coercivity of this material is also expressed in Tesla, how does the $y$-axis value of saturation magnetization compare with the $x$-axis value of coercivity? 
2. What is the value of the coercivity of this material in Oersteds? 
3. What is the value of the saturation magnetization of this grain-oriented steel in Gauss? 
4. Repeat this calculation for a sample of a neodymium-iron-boron $(\mathrm{Nd}_{2} \mathrm{Fe}_{14} \mathrm{~B})$ permanent magnet, whose coercive field is $700,000 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{m}$, if the saturation magnetization is 1.2 T. 

Give your answer as a tuple (coercivity in Tesla, coercivity in Oersteds, saturation magnetization in Gauss, coercivity in Tesla for Nd2Fe14B).The units of each required answer are (T, Oe, G, T), respectively.
response:
## Reasoning

**Setup.** The hysteresis loop is plotted with $B$ (in Tesla) on the y-axis and $H$ (in A/m) on the x-axis. To express the x-axis field in Tesla, we convert $H \to \mu_0 H$, using $\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \text{T·m/A}$.

**Part 1 — Coercivity in Tesla (grain-oriented steel).**
$$\mu_0 H_C = (4\pi\times10^{-7})(300) \approx 3.77\times10^{-4}\ \text{T}$$
The y-axis saturation value ($2.1$ T) **vastly exceeds** the x-axis coercivity value ($\approx 3.77\times10^{-4}$ T) — by a factor of $\sim 5570$. The loop is extremely narrow in the field direction.

**Part 2 — Coercivity in Oersteds.** Using $1\ \text{Oe} = \dfrac{1000}{4\pi}\ \text{A/m}$:
$$H_C = \frac{300}{1000/4\pi} = \frac{300\cdot 4\pi}{1000} \approx 3.77\ \text{Oe}$$

**Part 3 — Saturation magnetization in Gauss.** Using $1\ \text{T} = 10^{4}\ \text{G}$:
$$\mu_0 M_S = 2.1\ \text{T} = 2.1\times10^{4}\ \text{G} = 21000\ \text{G}$$

**Part 4 — Nd₂Fe₁₄B coercivity in Tesla.**
$$\mu_0 H_C = (4\pi\times10^{-7})(7.0\times10^{5}) \approx 0.88\ \text{T}$$
Here the loop is much "fatter" — the coercivity in Tesla (0.88 T) is comparable in magnitude to the saturation magnetization (1.2 T), consistent with a hard permanent magnet.

## Result

The requested tuple (coercivity in T, coercivity in Oe, saturation magnetization in G, Nd₂Fe₁₄B coercivity in T):

$$\boxed{(3.77\times10^{-4},\ 3.77,\ 21000,\ 0.88)}$$
